errors.english: Regarding the phrase, "Whatever the nature of destruction is," and so forth
errors.why: The lemma continues rgyun from the previous side: 'because [destruction] is of the nature of the cutting-off of the continuum', not 'whatever the nature of destruction is'.

errors.english: when we later explain the destruction of a pot and so forth
errors.why: 'chad par 'gyur ba here means 'when the pot etc. is cut off / ceases' (destruction as mere negation), not 'when we later explain'.

note: A sound rendering of the two kinds of destruction and the contradiction typology; the root-text lemma and one verb ('chad pa) are misread.

errors.english: perfectly knows the causes and the conditions for change
errors.why: The phrase completes rnam par dag par from the previous side: the causes and conditions for beings' becoming purified, not 'for change'.

fix.find: perfectly knows the causes and the conditions for change
fix.replace: perfectly knows the causes and the conditions for [beings'] becoming purified

note: Faithful rendering of the sutra passage on causes and conditions of defilement and purification and the Tathagata's absorptions, except the opening fragment.
Faithful translation of the five modes of Pratimoksa recitation and the reciter's, elder's and middle monk's duties.

errors.english: in the whole that possesses its parts
errors.why: ldan pa here is conjunction (samyoga): the whole in which conjunction is present, not 'the whole that possesses its parts'.

note: A careful rendering of the argument against variegated cognition by superimposition, with verses correctly set off; one technical term blurred.

errors.english: a momentary thing produces an effect that arises in a single moment
errors.why: 'Occurring in a single moment' qualifies the thing that produces, not the effect: 'a thing that exists for a single moment produces an effect'.

note: Generally accurate commentary on momentary production and the variant reading; one qualifier attached to the wrong noun.

errors.english: that would become its cause in the form of fire
errors.why: rgyu mer 'gyur most likely = rgyu med par 'gyur: if smoke arose from the non-fire Sakramurdhan, which is not its cause, the smoke would be causeless.

note: A good rendering of the fire/smoke specification argument; the Sakramurdhan consequence is probably misread.

errors.english: there are various instances of (conjunction) saṃyoga
errors.why: The opponent's claim is that there is a variegated conjunction of blue etc. (a single conjunction that is citra), not 'various instances of conjunction'.

errors.english: even if the object of sound is not diverse in nature
errors.why: sgra'i yul is the referent of the word: 'even if conjunction, the referent of the word [variegated], is not of variegated nature'; 'object of sound' loses the subject, conjunction.

errors.english: because of the (inherence) samavāya of many things in a single object of conjunction in a painting
errors.why: The Vaisesika notion is ekarthasamavaya: variegatedness is designated of the conjunction because it co-inheres in the same substrate, not 'inherence of many things in a single object of conjunction'.

note: Follows the anti-Vaisesika argument in outline, but the key technical relations (citra conjunction, ekarthasamavaya) are blurred in several places.

errors.english: These phenomena are not without afflictions, nor are they possessed of afflictions.
errors.why: The Tibetan says these dharmas are without afflictions and are not possessed of afflictions; the English adds a negation to the first clause.

fix.find: These phenomena are not without afflictions, nor are they possessed of afflictions.
fix.replace: These phenomena are without afflictions; they are not possessed of afflictions.

errors.why: 'byung ba here is going forth / deliverance (niryana), as in the following 'knowing all dharmas as leading forth', not 'origin'.

note: Readable rendering of the Aksayamati quotation on mindfulness of dharmas, but one clause is reversed and 'byung ba is taken as 'origin'.

errors.english: Through the pride of the lord of men
errors.why: ma bkur pa des (Skt. vimanena) = 'through that disrespect' shown by the nagas; it is not the king's pride.

fix.find: Through the pride of the lord of men
fix.replace: Through that disrespect, for the lord of men

errors.english: [note: original Sanskrit: "na vi mā nena", referring to a king]
errors.why: The Sanskrit is na vimanena 'by that dishonour'; it does not refer to a king.

errors.english: the lotus of his face lost its beauty
errors.why: The Tibetan (and its Sanskrit) are verses throughout; the English runs them as continuous prose.

note: Tibetan verses translated correctly in the main, but the opening misattributes the cause of the king's distress to his pride, and the verse is set as prose.

errors.english: karmic imprint or latent propensity that accords with both similar and dissimilar bodies
errors.why: The impression of habituation conforms [to the consciousness] in the case of both similar and dissimilar bodies; it does not 'accord with the bodies', and 'karmic' is not in the text.

note: Accurate on the whole for the argument that bodily change cannot explain differences of consciousness; one phrase is misattached.
